features.goal: Create a new book — name it, seed Sommaire + isolated Mort, and land in the editor.
key_architecture_choices: BookService owns the single atomic seed factory (exactly Sommaire + isolated locked Mort, 0 edges) — KR-001/KR-002.
Create flow orchestrated by useCreateBook through brain only: createBook (persist + book:created) -> openBook (book:opened) -> Router.navigate, guaranteeing listeners see a persisted book (KR-004).
BookService emits domain events (the mutation owner) so features never emit domain events directly.
Modal primitive owns scrim/Esc dismiss + focus capture/restore + focus trap, shared by all future dialogs.
Validation computed inline in NewBookDialog (no useEffect derived state, KR-013).
lessons_learned: react/no-unescaped-entities flags raw apostrophes in JSX text — use the typographic apostrophe in French copy.
Iteration 3 (cloud-first offline queue) blocked on the cloud-sync feature / CloudSyncService not yet existing; left planned.

features.goal: Render the open book as a navigable graph of node cards + labelled edges on a dot-grid canvas, with single-select and the « + Nœud » entry point — the primary editor surface (wireframe § 02).
key_architecture_choices: The canvas is a pure VIEW over BookService (KR-020): useOpenBook subscribes to the brain event bus and re-reads the persisted book via useSyncExternalStore — an external-store subscription, not a useEffect-synced mirror (KR-013).
Node mutation lives in BookService (the SSOT): addNode creates a free-floating node with a deterministic auto-layout slot (autoSlot, KR-023), persists, then emits node:created carrying the kind.
Selection is owned by the canvas (single source of truth, KR-024) and broadcast via node:selected{nodeId|null}; node-editor will react to it.
Pure, testable geometry (resolvePositions/resolveEdges): position-less nodes fall back to autoSlot; orphaned edges are dropped, never drawn to nowhere (KR-021).
node:created payload extended with a typed kind on the brain EventBus — a core domain event emitted by BookService, kept in brain (emitter-owned).
lessons_learned: Inheriting code-knowledge.json from another project left foreign KR ids (KR-001 = cloud-import-options) that collide with the gamebook's own KR namespace — the cross-project knowledge base needs a reset/namespacing before appending gamebook KRs.
Local pan/zoom is shippable without UIPreferencesService; only its PERSISTENCE must wait — split iteration 3 so the canvas is usable now (mirrors book-creation iter 3 deferring on CloudSyncService).
Canvas event flow: node cards / controls must stopPropagation on pointerdown+click so background pan/clear-selection only fire on true empty-canvas interactions.

features.goal: Edit a single leaf in a side panel beside the tree — description + end toggles now, with action/inventory/choices delegated to other features via brain seams.
key_architecture_choices: Promoted node selection to a brain SelectionService (single source of truth, KR-024): canvas + panel read via useSelectedNode and write via selection.select; the service is the sole node:selected emitter and clears on book:opened. This resolved the two-writer problem (panel ✕ deselect) that local canvas state could not.

node-editor is a HOST shell (KR-050) mounting action editors from a brain ActionRegistry (Open/Closed, KR-051) — adding an action type needs zero changes here; SegmentedControl options derive from the registry.
Fields bind directly to BookService.updateNode with no local mirror, and the panel subtree is keyed by node id, so selection swaps can't leak stale field state (KR-053/013).
End flags live on the node; effectiveKind/endLabel derive the FIN badge so canvas + panel reflect it from one source via node:updated (KR-054).

Shared view logic (useOpenBook, nodeTitle) and DS primitives (Toggle, SegmentedControl) promoted to brain (KR-109/110); the app shell composes canvas + panel without the features importing each other.
lessons_learned: A second writer of selection (the panel ✕) is the signal to promote selection from feature-local state to a brain SSOT — event-only broadcast is insufficient when two features both set it.

In RTL, drive selection through the UI (click a canvas card / + Nœud) rather than calling brain.selection.select directly — direct service mutations outside act() don't flush to the DOM before the next query.
Libellé du choix belongs on the incoming edge, not duplicated on the node — confirmed with the user to avoid a desync trap (KR-053-adjacent).

features.goal: Manage a node's outgoing choices — create a new child branch, relink to an existing node (cycles/convergence), and (later) per-choice hidden-prereq + countdown rules.
key_architecture_choices: New brain SlotRegistry (KR-066): node-editor reserves SLOT_NODE_EDITOR_CHOICES and renders the registered renderer (placeholder fallback); choice-linking registers its OutgoingChoices renderer at the composition root (App). Generalises the ActionRegistry OCP seam to arbitrary panel regions — neither feature imports the other.

Edge mutation in BookService (SSOT, KR-060): addChoiceBranch (child + choice edge, node:created then edge:created), addEdge (relink, cycles allowed, no node created), removeEdge (edge only, target node survives). edge:created payload extended with from/to + typed EdgeKind.
Mort's no-outgoing invariant enforced at the SSOT (KR-055/060), not just by hiding the UI section.
OutgoingChoices is a live VIEW via useOpenBook; the relink picker is local UI state (not derived-from-props, KR-013).
lessons_learned: When one feature must render inside another's panel, reach for a brain slot registry (host reserves, provider registers at the composition root) rather than a cross-feature import — mirrors ActionRegistry.

A slot renderer registered in a useEffect won't force the host to re-render (the registry has no subscribe); it works because the host re-renders for another reason (selection change) before the slot is needed — fine here, but a notify-on-register would be needed if a slot must appear without any other state change.
Pre-seed test fixtures BEFORE render() — a brain mutation after render (e.g. addChoiceBranch) updates subscribed views outside act() and triggers warnings.

iter 1: the libellé belongs on the EDGE (Edge.label), not the node — added BookService.updateEdge + an edge:updated event wired into useOpenBook's mutation list; the canvas already rendered edge.label ?? canvasLabel, so the new event made the canvas reflect labels live for free. A property that already exists on the model + a view that already reads it means the iteration is just the SSOT mutation path + its event.

iter 2: degenerate-edge guards (self-link, duplicate) belong at the SSOT (addEdge returns null + emits nothing), with the picker mirroring them only as a convenience — never UI-only, or a programmatic/API caller bypasses the invariant (the KR-067 pattern again). Edge IDENTITY for the duplicate guard is from+to+kind (not from+to): a relink and the future automatic flee to the same target are distinct legitimate convergence, so collapsing on from+to would forbid a valid future edge.

iter 2: a search filter over a live list is pure derived state — needle.toLowerCase() + Array.filter computed inline each render (KR-013), never a useEffect-synced mirror; reset the query on popover open/close/commit so a stale needle can't leak into the next open.

features.goal: List every persisted book on the home screen and open or delete any of them — the entry point to existing books, not just freshly created ones.
key_architecture_choices: New brain useBooks() view hook: a cached snapshot recomputed only on book:created/book:deleted via useSyncExternalStore (mirrors useOpenBook) — a live VIEW over BookService, never a useEffect mirror (KR-020/013/071).
BookService.deleteBook persists the removal before emitting book:deleted (KR-004/070), so the list re-reads a store without the book.

Composition-root seam (KR-072): LibraryScreen (book-library) owns the home chrome + list and receives the create affordance as a prop; App passes <CreateBookEntry/> (book-creation). Neither feature imports the other — same OCP pattern as ActionRegistry/SlotRegistry, applied to a sibling screen.
Deletion gated behind a confirmation dialog (dangerous action); shared Modal extended with confirmTone='error'. Pending-deletion target is local UI state, not derived from props (KR-013).
lessons_learned: When two sibling features must share a screen (list + create), compose at the app root by passing one's affordance as a prop — same isolation seam as the panel registries, no slot registry needed for a single static injection.
A getByRole regex like /Title/ also matches a delete button whose accessible name contains the title (« Supprimer « Title » ») — anchor the open-button query (/^Title/) to disambiguate.
book:deleted already existed on the EventBus before any emitter; wiring the emitter (deleteBook) closed the loop without a contract change.

iter 1: a rename needs a list-membership-agnostic refresh event — added book:updated to BOTH useBooks (BOOK_LIST_EVENTS) and useOpenBook (BOOK_MUTATION_EVENTS), since a rename changes list CONTENT (not membership) and an open editor's title. Enter-then-blur does NOT double-commit: React doesn't fire onBlur when the input unmounts on setEditing(false), so the inline-rename commit path is single regardless of Enter/blur/Esc.
iter 1: per-test localStorage.clear() must be added to every new describe block — a new BookService describe without its own beforeEach leaks prior tests' books into a listBooks() assertion.

iter 1: a 'deep copy' must deep-clone nested sub-objects, not shallow-spread the top level (BUG-002) — structuredClone is NOT defined in the jsdom jest env, so a JSON round-trip is the portable deep clone (and exact here, since the book is JSON-persisted anyway).

iter 2: filter+sort over the live useBooks snapshot must sort a COPY ([...books].sort) — the snapshot is the cached useSyncExternalStore reference, and mutating it in place breaks reference stability. Search/sort/sort-mode are local UI state, all derived inline (KR-013), no useEffect.

iter 2: a cross-route safety net (navigate home when the open book is deleted, KR-071) belongs at the COMPOSITION ROOT (App), not the feature — App subscribes to book:deleted and reads router.current() FRESH in the handler (no route dependency, no stale closure). Keeps cross-route navigation out of any single feature.

iter 2: SyncIndicator already uses role=status, so a second role=status (the search no-match line) makes getByRole('status') ambiguous — query the no-match copy by text, and reserve role=note for the empty state. A title span concatenated with a meta-count span has NO separator in textContent ('Zebra2 écrans…'), so extract a title with /^[^0-9]+/, not /\w+/.

iter 2: order-dependent sort tests need deterministic timestamps — drive updatedAt with jest.useFakeTimers()+setSystemTime around each createBook, then useRealTimers() before rendering/userEvent (createBrain is offline by default, so no transport timers to fight).

features.goal: Show the open book as an indented outline, switchable from the canvas, with selection shared so any row opens the node editor.
key_architecture_choices: buildOutline is a pure, view-agnostic DFS: choice edges nest; relink/flee, convergences and cycle back-edges become ↪ reference rows (visited set), never recursed, so a cyclic book can't loop (KR-080/061); unreachable nodes listed flat (KR-020).

Hoisted the shared editor top bar to brain/components/EditorTopBar (KR-109) and added a canvas ↔ outline SegmentedControl; a new src/EditorScreen shell owns the non-synced view-mode (KR-022) and swaps the body — tree-canvas became the canvas body only, CanvasTopBar removed.
Selection shared through the brain SelectionService (KR-024): the outline reads useSelectedNode and writes selection.select, so canvas + outline + panel never desync.
Outline derived inline with useMemo from the live book (KR-013/020); row badges/labels read the kind registry (KR-068); dangling targets flagged ⚠ (KR-021).
lessons_learned: Hoisting shared chrome (the top bar) out of the first feature that owned it into brain/components is the clean way to let a second view reuse it — the editor shell composes both views + the panel, features still don't import each other.

A cycle/convergence-safe traversal needs a visited set + reference rows BEFORE building any outline UI — bake it into the pure builder so the recursion guard is unit-tested, not discovered in the browser.

Hoisting the top bar kept every existing editor test green because EditorTopBar preserved the same roles/labels (heading title, « Ajouter un nœud », « N nœuds »); preserve accessible names when moving chrome.

iter 1: expand/collapse over a flat pre-order list is a pure helper (computeVisibleRows) — hide every later row deeper than a collapsed node until depth resumes; unit-test it, don't discover it in the browser (KR-080 spirit).

iter 1: adding a sibling disclosure button broke existing /Sommaire/ row queries (the disclosure aria-label « Replier « Sommaire » » also matched) — anchor row queries (/Sommaire$/) when a new button shares the node title, and remember KR-067 forbids relinking INTO the Sommaire/Mort (relink A→B between two children instead).

iter 2: a cross-view imperative action (« Centrer dans l'arbre » = outline asks the canvas to switch+centre) must be wired at the composition root with a shell-owned {nodeId, seq} prop, NOT an event bus — the canvas is unmounted while the outline shows, so an event fires before the target exists and is lost. A shell prop is read on the target's mount, surviving the view switch; a seq + consumed-seq ref makes repeats distinct yet ignores unrelated re-renders (KR-081).

iter 2: the inspector previews the FOCUSED/hovered row (local inspectedId), not the selection — so « Éditer » has a real job (commit the previewed node to selection) and row-click selection (the iter-1 contract + tests) stays intact. To test « Éditer » distinctly, hover a second row to preview-without-selecting, then assert the click changes selection.

iter 2: viewport centring is pure geometry given the transform (translate(x,y) scale(zoom), origin 0,0): x = W/2 − pointX·zoom. Read the container size from a ref in the effect (available after mount/paint); centre on the node's middle (pos + NODE_W/2, NODE_H/2).

features.goal: Configure a node's « Décor » action (prendre / écouter / fouiller) with, for « prendre », a takeable object — mounted into node-editor through the ActionRegistry without coupling the features.
key_architecture_choices: First real action-* feature: self-registers an ActionEditor with the brain ActionRegistry at the App composition root (registerActionDecor), proving the Open/Closed seam end-to-end — node-editor offers/mounts « Décor » with zero changes and no import (KR-050/051).

The shared ObjectEditor lives in brain/components (KR-052/109): décor « prendre » is its first consumer; PNJ/monster reuse it later without a cross-feature import. Controlled component — the owner persists onChange via BookService.
DecorEditor is a VIEW over BookService (KR-020): reads node.decor via useOpenBook, writes via updateNode; the takeable object carries a stable id minted lazily with createId (KR-003).

Domain model gained node.decor (DecorConfig) + GameObject; NodePatch carries decor so updateNode's text-only guard keeps it off structural screens (KR-055/090). createId is now exported from brain for feature id minting.
lessons_learned: The ActionRegistry seam built in node-editor's skeleton paid off: the first real action feature needed only a register call + an editor component, no node-editor change — validate a registry seam with its first real consumer.

A component shared by future siblings belongs in brain/components from its FIRST use (ObjectEditor), even when only one feature consumes it yet — putting it in the feature would force a cross-feature import later (KR-052/109).
Action config persists on the node document (node.decor) and rides the existing updateNode text-only guard for free — no new structural-screen handling needed (KR-055/090).

iter 1: when a skeleton field becomes a list (decor.object → decor.objects[]), migrate on read with a pure helper (takeablesOf) and canonicalise on the next write — never lose an old persisted shape (KR-090/116 spirit), and keep the deprecated field in the type with an @deprecated note.

iter 1: a per-item editor in a Modal wants DRAFT commit/cancel semantics (local state, keyed by item id, Enregistrer commits / Annuler discards) — distinct from the app's usual live-persist inline fields, but the right call for a modal so a cancelled NEW item never lands. Not a KR-013 violation: a one-shot draft init from props is legitimate editing state, not a useEffect-synced mirror.

iter 2: écouter/fouiller reuse the trap roll pattern wholesale — CHARACTERISTIQUE + DIFFICULTÉ + the shared brain OutcomesEditor — proving the réussite/échec rows were correctly extracted to brain (KR-109/091). The third consumer (after monster, trap) needed zero new shared code: a RevealEditor that just composes them. When a third feature reuses a brain primitive unchanged, the extraction was right.

iter 2: as a config grows facets (interaction + objects + reveal), collapse the writers into ONE writeDecor(patch) that re-emits the full canonical shape — per-facet writers that each spell out a partial object will eventually drop a sibling facet (here: editing objects must not lose reveal). One canonical writer + Partial patch is the safe shape.

iter 2: per-variant UI COPY (the écouter/fouiller reveal-field label + placeholder) belongs in the same closed-set Record as the variant's label (DECOR_INTERACTIONS extended from { label } to add revealLabel/revealPlaceholder), not a second `interaction === 'ecouter' ? …` ladder (KR-117).

features.goal: Configure a node's « PNJ » action — name + dialogue and an optional gift object — mounted into node-editor via the ActionRegistry, reusing the shared ObjectEditor.
key_architecture_choices: Second action-* feature: self-registers with the brain ActionRegistry at the App composition root (registerActionPnj) — the seam now mounts two editors (« Décor » + « PNJ ») with zero node-editor changes (KR-050/051).

Reuses the shared brain ObjectEditor for « donne un objet » (KR-052/109) — its SECOND consumer, imported from brain with no cross-feature import; validates the decision to place ObjectEditor in brain at its first use.

PnjEditor is a VIEW over BookService (KR-020): reads node.pnj via useOpenBook, normalises it once (DEFAULT_PNJ + destructure, mirroring the cleaned DecorEditor), writes via updateNode; the gift's stable id is minted lazily and preserved (KR-003).

Domain model gained node.pnj (PnjConfig); NodePatch carries pnj so updateNode's text-only guard keeps it off structural screens (KR-055/090). The gift toggle-off persists pnj without a gift (JSON drops the undefined value).
lessons_learned: A shared brain primitive proves its worth at the SECOND consumer: action-pnj reused ObjectEditor with a single brain import — the cross-feature-violation trap (importing a sibling feature's component) never materialised because it was placed in brain from the start.

Patch semantics: updateNode skips top-level undefined keys, but a nested undefined (pnj.gift) is fine — it reads as absent in memory and is dropped by JSON on persist, so a toggle-off cleanly removes a sub-object without a dedicated unset API.

Normalising the config once (DEFAULT_PNJ + destructure) from the start avoided the scattered-default smell DecorEditor had to be refactored out of — apply the cleaned pattern to each new action editor.

iter 1: a config node-reference (« mène à » → pnj.target) is the right skeleton for a non-choice screen change the canvas can't draw yet — capture the id + surface dangling (KR-021/063), defer the rendered edge to the dedicated action-edge path (KR-067), mirroring action-trap's deferred échec→Mort edge.

iter 1: a node-title shown both in a config picker AND on a canvas card collides in RTL `getByRole` — the card name is « Nœud #N — Title » so use an EXACT picker-button name (not /Title/) to disambiguate (cf. the outline /Sommaire$/ lesson).

features.goal: Configure a node's « Monstre » action — name + a player-facing reveal text per réussite/échec outcome — via the ActionRegistry, with a stub to save the monster to a reusable library.
key_architecture_choices: Third action-* feature: self-registers with the brain ActionRegistry at the App composition root (registerActionMonster) — the seam mounts three editors with zero node-editor changes (KR-050/051).

réussite/échec — the only semantic outcomes/colours — modelled as a brain ROLL_OUTCOMES registry (Record<RollOutcome,{label,tone}>, KR-117/091), placed in brain because trap/skill-roll editors will reuse it (KR-109, the ObjectEditor lesson applied pre-emptively to a domain concept). MonsterEditor derives both outcome rows from it.
MonsterEditor is a VIEW over BookService (KR-020), normalised once; monster config lives on node.monster, NodePatch carries it (text-only guard keeps it off structural screens, KR-055/090).

Monster library stubbed via a new monster:savedToLibrary EventBus event (wired, unconsumed) — like book:deleted existed before its emitter. Added ariaLabel to the shared Field so Badge-captioned fields keep an accessible name.
lessons_learned: Applied the ObjectEditor placement lesson to a DOMAIN CONCEPT, not just a component: réussite/échec is domain-wide, so its registry went straight to brain — future trap/skill-roll editors reuse it with no cross-feature import.

When a Badge captions a field (semantic colour) the input loses its accessible name — add an ariaLabel rather than leaning on the placeholder; caught in self-review by making the outcome fields queryable.
A closed-set Record (KR-117) doubles as the loop source for the UI: mapping ROLL_OUTCOMES keys renders both outcome rows, so adding an outcome would be one entry — no second edit site.

iter 1: the 'extract to brain at the 2nd consumer' rule fired twice more — the value Stepper and the TargetPicker moved to brain/components when action-monster became their second consumer (after action-pnj), refactoring pnj in the SAME slice (behaviour-preserving, tests stay green). Same trigger as ObjectEditor/OutcomesEditor (KR-109).

iter 1: a shared brain component needs its feature-specific copy parameterised — TargetPicker gained label/emptyLabel props so PNJ « mène à » and monster victoire/fuite reuse one component; bumping per-stepper aria-labels off the `label` prop keeps several Steppers on one screen distinct (and required updating the pnj test queries).

features.goal: Configure a node's « Piège » action — description + réussite/échec reveal texts + whether failure is lethal — via the ActionRegistry, reusing the shared outcome editor.
key_architecture_choices: Fourth and final action-* feature: self-registers with the brain ActionRegistry (registerActionTrap) — node-editor now offers all four action types with zero changes (KR-050/051), validating the seam end-to-end.

Extracted a shared brain OutcomesEditor (KR-109) at the SECOND consumer of the réussite/échec rows (monster→trap): both editors render outcomes from one component derived from ROLL_OUTCOMES (KR-117/091); MonsterEditor refactored to use it. Same trigger as the ObjectEditor extraction.
TrapEditor is a VIEW over BookService (KR-020), normalised once; trap config on node.trap, NodePatch carries it (text-only guard, KR-055/090).
The « échec sanctionné » variant is a fatal boolean capturing intent; the automatic échec→Mort edge is deferred to the dedicated combat/trap path, not the manual edge API (KR-067/092).
lessons_learned: The 'extract to brain at the 2nd consumer' rule now has two confirmations (ObjectEditor, OutcomesEditor) — when a second feature needs the same rows, refactor the first to the shared component in the same slice; behaviour-preserving and the tests stay green.

All four action editors landed by composing the SAME seams (ActionRegistry + BookService VIEW + shared brain primitives) — the skeleton's investment in node-editor's host seam + brain registries paid back four times with near-zero node-editor churn.

A boolean flag (trap.fatal) is the right skeleton stand-in for a deferred structural mechanic (the automatic →Mort edge): capture intent on the node now, wire the edge when the dedicated path is built (KR-067).

iter 1: a DOMAIN closed set goes straight to brain as a registry — CHARACTERISTICS joined ROLL_OUTCOMES in brain (KR-117) at the trap skill roll, fulfilling the décor-iter-1 note that the caractéristique catalog extracts at the 2nd consumer; the select derives from it.

iter 1: widen a shared type rather than fork it — making SkillRoll.failureText optional let trap (réussite/échec via outcomes) and décor (échec via failureText) share ONE roll shape instead of two near-duplicates; the additive optional field broke nothing in décor.

iter 1: don't bundle a product change into an unrelated slice — switching décor's free-text caractéristique to the new closed select changes décor UX, so it was deferred to a décor iteration (registry left brain-ready) rather than smuggled into the trap slice.

features.goal: Make the app local-first and sync-aware: every write persists locally first, optionally pushes to a cloud transport in the background, and a status pill reflects the sync state.
key_architecture_choices: CloudSyncService is a Decorator over PersistenceService (Liskov, KR-011/093): createBrain wraps the local store with it and feeds it to BookService, so every feature is sync-aware with ZERO changes — the cleanest demonstration of the interface-first persistence boundary.

Local-first (KR-004): set writes local synchronously, then pushes in the background (idle→syncing→synced/error); a failed push keeps the local write. With no transport the store is offline (local-only) and emits sync:status only on a real change — so wrapping is transparent and the existing 99 tests needed no edits.

useSyncStatus is an external-store subscription over the new sync:status event (KR-013); the cloud-sync feature's SyncIndicator is a VIEW deriving label/tone from a SyncStatus Record (KR-117), mounted once by App over both routes.
SyncStatus is a brain type and CloudTransport keeps the real backend swappable; the Cloudflare worker client + offline queue + reconciliation are deferred to iterations 1–3.
lessons_learned: An interface-first persistence boundary pays off exactly when a decorator is introduced: wrapping local with CloudSyncService changed one line in createBrain and nothing in any feature — the Liskov contract held.

Default-inert infrastructure keeps a big change safe: with no transport the wrapper is a transparent synchronous pass-through (no async, no events), so 99 existing tests stayed green without touching them — design the default so the new layer is invisible until opted into.
This closes the 0.1.x MVP tier: all eleven features have a walking skeleton; the next tier (0.2.x / V1) is iteration 1 of each, in build order.

iter 1: the cloud transport is chosen by BUILD/PRODUCTION TARGET at the composition root (main.tsx) — the local build wires a localStorage-backed LocalStorageTransport (fake remote) so the full machinery runs serverless; Cloudflare swaps a worker-backed one via the same interface later. Keeping createBrain transport-optional kept every existing test transparent (offline).

iter 1: a sync decorator that adopts a pulled value must write the UNDERLYING store, never its own decorated set — otherwise it re-pushes what it just pulled (echo loop). LWW reconciliation on book:opened emits book:updated so open views re-read (KR-094).

iter 1: debouncing the push changed set()'s timing (push is no longer synchronous), so the CloudSyncService tests moved to a debounceMs:0 + macrotask-flush pattern; status 'syncing' is still set synchronously on write so the UI feels instant.
This closes the 0.2.x / V1 tier: every feature has its iteration 1; the next tier (0.3.x / V2) is iteration 2 of each, in build order.
